other_failure_modes.name: categorical_as_continuous_in_nn
other_failure_modes.description: Label-encoded categorical variables are passed directly into a neural network as continuous numerical features (after standardization), which falsely implies an ordinal relationship. Embeddings or one-hot encoding should be used instead.

other_failure_modes.name: ignoring_native_cat_handling
other_failure_modes.description: The agent uses models that support native categorical features (CatBoost, LightGBM) but passes the data as a standardized float32 numpy array without specifying categorical feature indices, degrading the models' ability to handle categorical data optimally.

other_failure_modes.name: cv_target_leakage_in_oof_features
other_failure_modes.description: The agent uses the exact same K-Fold split object (same seed and splits) for generating out-of-fold features (Target Encoding, Text predictions) as for the final model cross-validation. This leaks the validation fold's target information into the training folds' features, resulting in an overly optimistic CV score.

other_failure_modes.name: feature_leakage_in_group_aggregations
other_failure_modes.description: Group-by aggregations (mean/std of numerical features) and TF-IDF vectorizers are fitted on the entire training set before cross-validation splitting, leaking the feature distributions of validation folds into the training folds.

summary: The agent provides a comprehensive pipeline with extensive feature engineering and model diversity. However, it fails to tune the ensemble weights, treats categorical variables as continuous in the neural network, ignores native categorical support in tree models, and introduces target leakage into the CV process by reusing the same folds for out-of-fold feature generation.
